blocks.text: Setting up your credit analyst workspace in Notion

Start by creating a master database for your deal pipeline. Use the /database command to initialize a table view. Add properties for Deal Name, Stage, Borrower, Credit Rating, and Due Date. Use a Select property for the deal stage, such as Initial Review, Underwriting, Committee, or Closing. This gives you a clear view of your current workload without switching between multiple apps.

Credit analysts often struggle with document retrieval. Create a page for each borrower to store their financial statements, tax returns, and legal agreements. Use the /file command to upload PDFs directly into the page. To track covenants, create a separate database linked to your borrower page using a Relation property. This allows you to monitor compliance dates and trigger alerts for upcoming reporting requirements.

items: Use Lazur to explain complex Notion database formulas when you are stuck.
Ask Lazur to point at the correct menu to export your report as a PDF.
Dictate your meeting notes directly into Notion using the fn key.
Have Lazur research market data in Chrome and summarize it for your credit memo.
Use Lazur to guide you through setting up advanced database filters.

blocks.text: Administrative tasks like updating deal trackers often consume half your day. Use Notion templates to standardize your credit memo structure. Go to the top right of your database, click the arrow next to New, and create a template. This ensures every deal follows the same format, saving you time on repetitive setup. If you need to find a specific setting, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. Lazur will draw a circle around the button for you.
Best practices for Notion on Mac

items: Always keep your app updated via Notion > Check for Updates.
Use ⌘ P to open the search bar and jump to any page in seconds.
Use ⇧ ? to view all keyboard shortcuts and improve your typing speed.
Keep your database views clean by using filters to hide closed deals.
Use toggles to hide long sections of financial analysis for a cleaner view.

blocks.text: You likely pull data from Bloomberg or S&P Capital IQ. While you cannot directly import live terminals into Notion, you can embed Google Sheets or export CSV files. Use /embed to bring in shared spreadsheets. This keeps your model data visible alongside your qualitative analysis. If you are struggling with a specific formula, ask Lazur to explain the syntax while you have the cell selected.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for sensitive financial data?
faq.answer: Notion provides enterprise-grade security, but always check your firm's internal compliance policies regarding where client documents can be hosted.

faq.question: How do I speed up my workflow in Notion?
faq.answer: Use keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ N for a new page and / to quickly insert blocks. Using Lazur to dictate notes or guide you through setup will also save significant time.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with the Notion desktop app?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works with any app on your Mac, including the Notion desktop app. You can ask questions about your screen, dictate text, or get guidance on interface elements.

faq.question: What is the best way to track deal status?
faq.answer: Use a Board view in a Notion database. Group your deals by a status property, such as Prospect, Underwriting, or Approved, to visualize your pipeline.
